faults.title: Engine will not start
causes: Blade control lever not held against the handlebar
Fuel valve OFF, or out of fuel
Spark plug fouled, worn, wrongly gapped or wet (flooded)
Fuel filter, carburetor, ignition or valve fault
checks: Hold the blade control lever against the handlebar while pulling
Turn the fuel valve ON; check the fuel level
Drain and refill with fresh fuel (86+ octane, up to E10)
Remove the plug: dry it if wet, regap to 0.7–0.8 mm or replace
If it still won't start, the carburetor, ignition or valves need a dealer

faults.title: Loss of power or stalling in grass
causes: Grass too tall or wet for the cut
Carburetor, fuel filter, ignition or valve fault
checks: Raise the cutting height, take a narrower swath, slow down, or mow more often
Clean under the deck
Clean or replace the air filter
Refuel with fresh fuel

faults.title: Excessive vibration
causes: Grass or debris packed under the deck
Blades bent, damaged or out of balance
checks: Stop the engine and clean under the deck
Torque the blade bolts to 49–59 N·m
Inspect the blades; bent blades go to a dealer for inspection
After a strike on a hard object, check the blade holder and have the crankshaft checked
faults.safety: Turn the fuel valve OFF and pull the spark plug cap before touching the blades or tilting the mower. Tilt with the fuel cap side up.

faults.title: Engine and blades don't stop quickly when the lever is released
causes: Blade control cable out of adjustment
checks: Do the blade control check: start outdoors, release the lever, the engine should stop quickly
If it doesn't, stop using the mower and take it to a dealer
faults.safety: Don't use the mower if the blades keep turning after the lever is released.

faults.title: Self-propel weak or not driving
causes: Smart Drive cable out of adjustment
checks: Check the Smart Drive adjuster position
Have the Smart Drive cable adjusted and the pinion gears greased by a dealer

faults.title: White or blue smoke at start-up
causes: Oil put in the cylinder for storage (normal, clears quickly)
Mower tilted the wrong way (oil into the air filter or muffler)
checks: Let it run; smoke from storage oil clears
Tilt only with the fuel cap side up
Check the oil level; drain to the correct level if overfilled

faults.title: Low or dirty oil
causes: Oil not changed at the interval
checks: Check oil before every use
Change oil: first month or 5 h, then every 6 months or 50 h (every 25 h under heavy load or heat)

faults.title: Starter rope hard to pull or kicks back
causes: Blade blocked by grass or debris
Bent crankshaft or damaged blade after a strike
checks: Clean under the deck (engine off, plug cap off)
Make sure the blade control lever is fully held against the handlebar
Have a dealer check after any blade strike
faults.safety: Turn the fuel valve OFF and pull the spark plug cap before touching the blades or tilting the mower. Tilt with the fuel cap side up.

faults.title: Grass bag not filling
causes: Blades dull, worn or wrong blades
checks: Use less Smart Drive pressure
Empty or wash the bag
Set both height levers to the same position
Clean the deck
Sharpen or replace the blades
Set the Clip Director to BAG

sequence.name: Pre-use checks
sequence.desc: Check oil, blades and blade bolts, rear shield, grass bag, and the area for debris.

sequence.name: Start
sequence.desc: Fuel valve ON, hold the blade control lever against the handlebar, pull the starter until resistance then briskly. Auto choke handles the cold start.

sequence.name: Warm-up
sequence.desc: Run a cold engine at least 3 minutes before stopping it (longer below 21 °C) so the auto choke opens fully.

sequence.name: Mowing
sequence.desc: Push the Smart Drive control to drive; more pressure is faster. Clip Director set to BAG or MULCH.
sequence.ends: Area finished or bag near 90% full

sequence.name: Stop
sequence.desc: Release the blade control lever: the flywheel brake stops the engine and blades. Turn the fuel valve OFF when finished.

checks.name: Before each use
checks.why: Catches blade damage and low oil before they cause damage.
steps: Check the engine oil level
Inspect the blades and blade bolts
Check the rear shield and grass bag for wear
Do the blade control check: released lever stops the engine quickly

checks.name: Oil change
checks.why: Small engines run hot and thin the oil quickly.
steps: First month or 5 h, then every 6 months or 50 h; every 25 h in heavy load or heat
Fuel valve OFF; drain warm, tilting onto the right side
Refill 0.35–0.40 L SAE 10W-30 (API SJ+); don't overfill
Never use non-detergent or 2-stroke oil

checks.name: Air filter
checks.why: A clogged filter costs power and raises fuel use.
steps: Clean after the first 25 h, then every 6 months or 50 h (more often in dust)
Replace every 2 years or 150 h
Tap it out or blow from the inside at no more than 207 kPa; don't brush

checks.name: Spark plug
steps: Replace every 2 years or 150 h (NGK BPR5ES)
Gap 0.7–0.8 mm; bend only the side electrode
Thread in by hand, then 1/2 turn for new or 1/8–1/4 turn for reused; 20 N·m

checks.name: Blade service
checks.why: Dull or unbalanced blades tear grass and cause vibration.
steps: Fuel OFF, plug cap off, tilt fuel cap side up
Hold the blade with thick gloves; 14 mm 6-point socket
Replace blades as a set with Honda bolts and special washers
Torque 49–59 N·m
Replace the blade holder if damaged or after a hard strike

checks.name: Dealer service items
checks.why: Items the owner's manual leaves to a dealer.
steps: Valve clearance: 0.10 ± 0.02 mm intake and exhaust (cold)
Flywheel brake pad
Smart Drive cable adjustment, pinion gear grease, axle bearings
Fuel tank and filter cleaning; fuel lines every 2 years
Spark arrester (if fitted) every 100 h

checks.name: Storage (over 3–4 weeks)
checks.why: Stale fuel is the most common cause of no-start in spring.
steps: Fuel valve OFF and run the carburetor dry, or use stabilizer
Change the oil; put about 5 cc of oil in the cylinder, pull the starter several times, then pull slowly to resistance
Clean the deck; don't hose near the air cleaner or exhaust
Store level, ventilated, away from flames, under a breathable cover

reference.name: Specifications

reference.name: Torques and clearances

defects.name: Uneven cut or scalping
defects.looks: Patches cut too short or down to soil; ridges between passes.
isolate: Check both height levers are on the same position
Check tyre/wheel condition and that the mower sits level

causes.cause: Front and rear height levers at different settings
causes.fix: Set both to the same position

causes.cause: Cutting too low on uneven ground

causes.fix: Replace blades as a set; check the holder

defects.src: Honda HRN216VKU owner's manual; general mowing practice

defects.name: Torn, brown grass tips
defects.looks: Ragged tips that turn brown a day or two after mowing.
isolate: Look closely at a cut leaf: a clean cut is straight, a torn one is frayed

causes.fix: Slow down or raise the cut

defects.name: Strips of uncut grass
defects.looks: Narrow uncut lines between passes or within a pass.

causes.fix: Overlap each pass by a few centimetres

defects.src: Honda HRN216VKU owner's manual; general mowing practice

defects.name: Clumps of clippings left on the lawn
defects.looks: Rows or piles of clippings, especially when mulching.
isolate: Check whether it happens only in tall or wet grass

causes.cause: Taking off too much at once
causes.fix: Remove no more than about a third of the blade length per cut
Mow when dry or use BAG
